quizzes.title: CSS Basics Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Introduction, Selectors, Specificity & Inheritance, Box Model, Color, Background & Typography.

questions.prompt: Which selector targets the element with id="menu"?
questions.explanation: # selects by id and . selects by class. A plain name selects an element type.

questions.prompt: Which selector has the highest specificity?
questions.explanation: An id counts the most: #nav a is (1,0,1), .menu a is (0,1,1), nav a is (0,0,2), and a is (0,0,1).

questions.prompt: From the inside out, what is the order of the box model?
questions.explanation: Content is surrounded by padding, then the border, and finally the margin outside.

questions.prompt: With the default box-sizing (content-box), how wide is the box in total (not counting margin)?
questions.explanation: Total = 200 content + 2 x 20 padding + 2 x 5 border = 250px.
All three rules match, but the id selector has the highest specificity, so red wins.
questions.code: Hi

questions.prompt: Complete the property that makes the text red.
questions.explanation: color sets the text colour. background-color would change the background instead.

quizzes.title: Layout & Responsive Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Layout & Responsive Design, Flexbox in Depth, CSS Grid in Depth, Spacing & Responsive Design.

questions.prompt: Which declaration turns an element into a flex container?
questions.explanation: display: flex on the parent makes its children flex items.

questions.prompt: Which property centers flex items along the main axis?
questions.explanation: justify-content works along the main axis (a row by default). align-items works on the cross axis.

questions.prompt: Which line makes as many grid columns as fit, each at least 160px wide?
questions.explanation: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(160px, 1fr)) creates a responsive grid without any media query.

questions.prompt: The row has three equal boxes. What does flex-grow: 2 do to the second box?
options: It shrinks to half its size
It gets twice as much of the free space as each other box
It moves to a second row
questions.explanation: flex-grow shares the leftover space in proportion. A value of 2 gets double the share of a box with 1.

options: Hides the page on all screens
Applies the rules only on screens 600px or wider
Applies the rules only on screens 600px wide or narrower
questions.explanation: max-width means "up to this width", which is how you style phones and small windows.

questions.prompt: Complete the property that lets flex items move onto new lines.
questions.explanation: flex-wrap: wrap lets items go to the next line instead of squeezing into one row.

quizzes.title: Effects & Advanced Checkpoint
quizzes.description: Covers: Pseudo-class & Pseudo-Element, Transitions & Animations, Variables, Units & Modern Functions.

questions.prompt: Which pseudo-class styles an element while the mouse is over it?
questions.explanation: :hover is for the mouse pointer. :active is while pressed, :focus is for keyboard focus.

questions.prompt: How do you use a CSS variable named --brand?
questions.explanation: Define it with --brand: value; and read it with var(--brand).

questions.prompt: Which properties are best to animate for smooth performance?
questions.explanation: transform and opacity can be animated by the GPU without recalculating the layout.

questions.prompt: What happens when the user hovers over the button?
options: The background fades from blue to orange over 0.3 seconds
questions.explanation: The transition on .btn makes the change gradual instead of instant.
A variable can be overridden inside a smaller scope. .b sets its own --size.

questions.prompt: Complete the at-rule that defines the steps of an animation.
questions.explanation: @keyframes names an animation and describes what happens at each step.
